findings.summary: The mandatory VM lab procedure cannot compose with its physical-only #83 prerequisite.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/67/intent.md:8,76-81 requires consumers on fl-a/fl-b; design.md:156-162 prescribes the VM lab and says #83 host profile remains a prerequisite. At dependency 67862ad667ac3121b453c9227cef1e8ec5248138, #83 spec S1 and design.md:19-42 require physical-boottime-v1 and explicitly refuse existing lab VMs; a qualification run cannot make these VMs supported. #84 design.md:224-227 already records the compatible before-#83/after-#83 distinction. Thus this plan has no executable success path under its own stated composed prerequisite.
findings.fix: Add an explicit whoever-lands-second composition in #67 only: before #83 lands, any VM evidence is limited to the old supported/test baseline and cannot certify physical clock admission; after #83 lands, gateway-up/test on these VMs refuses before publication/mutation, and the two-node success/restart qualification runs on two admitted physical workload hosts. Preserve one manually provisioned node-pinned gateway and no node-loss failover. State what physical and minimum-kernel #84 evidence is actually required rather than imply VM checks satisfy it. Add fake preflight fixtures for excluded VM refusal and admitted two-node setup, and label the future real evidence by host/profile.

findings.summary: The plan omits the host NFS-client dependency needed for the static NFS PV to mount.
findings.evidence: intent.md:61-68 explicitly observes that lab VMs lack mount.nfs and that their kernel NFS-client support is unverified. scripts/guest/provision.sh:10 installs neither nfs-common nor equivalent client tooling. design.md:63-69 uses an in-tree NFS PV, and :103-110/:130-151 define setup/files/tests without any host-client installation or fail-closed helper/module preflight. Building a Ganesha/tunnel image under scripts/dev does not supply the kubelet host mount namespace. Official Kubernetes source pkg/volume/nfs/nfs.go:221-227 passes type nfs to the host mounter (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/v1.34.0/pkg/volume/nfs/nfs.go). A normal provisioned lab node therefore cannot perform the promised consumer mount.
findings.fix: Specify the supported host NFSv4.1 client package/helper and kernel capability prerequisites on both consumer nodes. Either add explicit lab provisioning changes (including scripts/guest/provision.sh in the files list), or document an operator-installed prerequisite and make up/test refuse before creating/publicizing resources when the actual kubelet host helper or kernel client is absent. Record client versions in qualification and add missing-helper/missing-client-support fixtures plus the future real mount through each node-local proxy.

findings.summary: The stable-ACK qualification needs an ordering/error oracle beyond process-kill checksum survival.
findings.evidence: design.md:39-42 requires durable shutdown-independent ordering, but its concrete S2 evidence at :143 and Lab :156-158 is stable-write/COMMIT/fsync plus SIGKILL and byte verification. Killing Ganesha on the same node does not discard the backing filesystem kernel page cache; an erroneous server that calls pwritev then returns stable success before fsync can pass that restart/checksum test. Existing #84 tests establish durability of completed block writes, not that Ganesha waited for its filesystem sync before an NFS stable reply. Official Ganesha VFS file.c:1322-1340 and :1570-1614 show the actual boundary: pwritev, conditional fsync before done_cb for stable WRITE, and fsync status for COMMIT (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nfs-ganesha/nfs-ganesha/next/src/FSAL/FSAL_VFS/file.c). The draft needs a concrete fixture that fails when this required ordering is omitted.
findings.fix: Extend the accepted pinned-release qualification with observed filesystem-sync-to-NFS-reply ordering and deterministic delayed/failed sync cases for both stable WRITE and COMMIT. For example, gate the selected release’s actual fsync/fdatasync boundary and show no stable-success reply until successful completion; return an injected sync error and assert no stable-success reply. Include a negative candidate/fixture that skips the wait so the oracle demonstrably fails. Retain SIGKILL/reclaim tests and #84 block conformance; no new replica rule, node-loss test or shared-lab execution is required for this plan review.
